equivalent.why: `attachedTarget` and `boundListener` are assigned as a pair in attach and cleared as a pair in detach and in the rollback, so the two fields are never one defined and one not; `||` and `&&` agree on every state that can occur.
with the target check gone, `listener === undefined` still decides, and the listener is undefined exactly when the target is, because the two are set and cleared together.
with the listener check gone, `target === undefined` still decides, and the target is undefined exactly when the listener is, because the two are set and cleared together.
an empty catch makes `matchesSource` return `undefined`, and its one caller negates that the same way it negates `false`: the event is refused as `source` either way.
an empty catch makes `matchesOrigin` return `undefined`, and both callers negate that the same way they negate `false`: the message is refused as `origin` either way.
calling an undefined handler throws a TypeError inside the try that isolates every handler call, so the guard saves a throw the catch would swallow, not a behaviour.

an object without `createPolicy` is returned as the factory, and the `createPolicy` call then throws a TypeError inside the try in `resolvePolicy`, whose catch sets the policy to `null` — the value the guard leads to.
`undefined.createPolicy` throws a TypeError inside the same try, whose catch sets the policy to `null` — the value the branch sets when there is no API.
the pattern is anchored at the start only, so one class character and a run of them match exactly the same strings: whatever follows the first character is not looked at.
an empty string reaches `new URL('')`, which throws, and the relative-path pattern does not match it, so the same `false` comes out of the catch; the early return only saves the parse.
